blockers.evidence: src/wpc/se.h names SE_BOARDID_520_5242_00 the 'Lord of The Rings 19 LED Board' and lotrGameData declares it. src/wpc/se.c writes CORE_MODOUT_LAMP0 + 80, + 88 and + 96 masked 0x07, and sets core_set_pwm_output_led_vfd(CORE_MODOUT_LAMP0 + 80, 3 * 8, CORE_MODOUT_LED, 4.f / 2.f) in the lotr-only branch. The retained VPW and JPSalas scripts both assign lamps 81-99.
blockers.summary: Nineteen playfield LEDs on board 520-5242-00 are driven by the ROM at public lamp addresses 81-99 and are not enumerated, so they carry no placement.
blockers.why_not_fixed_here: controllers/pinmame/whitestar.json caps pinmame.output.lamp at 1-80. Widening a shared controller profile affects every Whitestar game and is a maintainer decision.

blockers.summary: 50 placements are observed rather than validated, for five distinct reasons: 29 because fewer than all three retained recreations agree on them, 13 because they are projections onto a co-located anchor and a projection is never promoted however well the tables agree, 3 because the coordinate is a per-axis median of tables that disagreed, so every contributing table appears in its source_refs while none of them holds the published position, 1 because the coordinate is a centroid of co-located bodies inside a single table, which involves no disagreement at all, and 4 because no retained table separates the printed back-panel insert pairs, so the published coordinate is the pair rather than the bulb. reason_partition names which rows each reason covers; support_partition counts how many tables appear in each row's source_refs, which for the computed rows is a count of contributors and not a count of agreement. Both are disjoint and sum to the total.

blockers.summary: 15 devices are printed with a position on the DR.7 location drawing but modelled by no retained recreation, so they carry no spatial evidence at all. They are not recorded as not_applicable: the manual places them, and asserting otherwise on the manual's own authority would be false.

computed_coordinates.resolution: DR.7 prints '25' three times, once beside each of coils 9, 10 and 11, all marked Red. FLASH: POPS X3 is three physical bulbs at the three pop bumpers, so each table legitimately picked a different one. Placed at the centroid of the three bumper positions with physical.quantity 3.

DR.7 states flashers 26 and 27 are on the Back Panel and prints 27 (Clear) at the top right. All three tables place it in that corner but spread x 0.888-0.932 and y 0.033-0.074, just outside the agreement threshold; the per-axis median is taken.
DR.7 places 30 (Clear) on the right rail immediately beside coil 21, Sword Lock Release. All three tables agree on that region within 0.053; the per-axis median is taken.
All three tables agree on y within 0.008 but spread x from 0.182 to 0.266 for the Top VUK. DR.4 places 41 in the upper-left; the per-axis median is taken.

coordinate_convention.precision: at most six fractional decimal places

excluded_object_classes: JPSalas f<N>l helper Lights, which are non-positional and parked together at one coordinate
primitive origins left at (0,0) because their transform is baked into mesh vertices

method.artwork_caveat: The VPW table identifies itself as 'Lord Of The Rings - Valinor Edition' with original artwork, so where its insert layout departs from the printed diagrams that is an artwork difference, not an error.
method.rule: A placement is validated only when all three retained tables agree on it within the threshold; anything supported by fewer is observed.
method.why_all_three: Independence between the three recreations is unestablished and the two available signals disagree. Measured: the JPSalas and Hanibal tables agree with each other to within 0.0155 on every lamp both model, while either differs from VPW by up to 0.187. Documented: VPW credits an 'EBIsLit - Baseline playfield scan' and JPSalas records its playfield as 'based on Ebislit's playfield', while Hanibal declares only "4k Mod" in its title and names no baseline. The measured clustering pairs JPSalas with Hanibal; the documented ancestry pairs VPW with JPSalas. Requiring all three removes the need to guess which signal describes the lineage.
